blocks.content:
The President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College consisting of:
• Elected members of both Houses of Parliament
• Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
• Elected members of Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry

Nominated members do NOT participate in the election.
Voting System:
• Proportional Representation
• Single Transferable Vote
• Secret Ballot
Nominated members do NOT participate in the election.

rows: Elected Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha)
Elected Members of State Legislative Assemblies
Elected Members of Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry
Nominated Members of Parliament & Legislative Assemblies

items: Nominated members of Parliament and State Assemblies do NOT participate in the Presidential election.
Only the elected members of Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry are included among Union Territories.
The voting mechanism strictly uses Proportional Representation with a Single Transferable Vote and Secret Ballot.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President of India is elected indirectly by an Electoral College under Article 54.
The Electoral College comprises elected members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies.
Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry are included in the Electoral College.
Nominated members from any house or assembly are excluded from participating in the election.
The voting system follows Proportional Representation by means of a Single Transferable Vote through a Secret Ballot.
